cards.explanation: The answer is True. Verse 30 puts it in order. As soon as Laban, Rebekah's brother, saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and heard her words, he went and found the man. I think a brother who spots jewelry on his sister's wrists is going to get moving. Ring first, then he goes to find the man.

The answer is blessed by the LORD. Laban says, “Come, you who are blessed by the LORD…” (verse 31). That's how he greets a stranger standing out by a spring with his camels. Not a bad welcome for a man who just showed up.

The answer is False. The opposite is true. Laban says, “Why are you standing out here? I have prepared the house and a place for the camels.” (verse 31). The house is ready before the man says a word about why he came. Then the camels are unloaded, and straw and feed are brought to them (verse 32). I think Laban would pass any surprise-guest test.

The answer is False. He holds off. The meal is right in front of him, and he says, “I will not eat until I have told you what I came to say.” (verse 33). Laban answers, “Please speak.” The talking comes first and the eating comes after.

The answer is everything he owns. The servant says, “…my master has given him everything he owns.” (verse 36). Abraham's wife Sarah had a son in her old age, and that's Isaac, the one the servant is finding a wife for. Everything is a whole lot more than half.

The answer is to his father's house and family. Abraham told his servant, “…you shall go to my father’s house and to my kindred to take a wife for my son.” (verse 38). The Canaanites were ruled out, so family was the direction. That's exactly where the servant ends up, at Rebekah's family.

The answer is True. Verse 41 has it. Abraham says, “…if they refuse to give her to you, then you will be released from my oath.” The servant isn't stuck forever if the answer is no. He's also telling Rebekah's family this up front, which is honest of him.

The answer is “Whose daughter are you?” The servant says that to Rebekah in verse 47. She answers, “The daughter of Bethuel son of Nahor, whom Milcah bore to him.” Bethuel is her father. Only then does he put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.
The answer is go somewhere else. The servant says, “…if not, let me know, so that I may go elsewhere.” (verse 49). He asks for a plain answer, yes or no. Either way, he's ready to move on.

The answer is the LORD. Laban and Bethuel answer, “This is from the LORD; we have no choice in the matter.” (verse 50). Bethuel is Rebekah's father. They say it came from the LORD, not from the servant or anyone else.

The answer is True. Verse 53 says he brought out jewels of silver and gold, and articles of clothing, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave precious gifts to her brother and her mother. Rebekah's gifts get named first, though. Silver, gold AND clothing? I'd need a second mustache just to carry that much!

The answer is a little more time with her. Her brother and mother say, “Let the girl remain with us ten days or so. After that, she may go.” (verse 55). They aren't saying no. They're asking for a little more time before she leaves.
The answer is False. He holds his ground. In verse 56 he replies, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success.” Then he adds, “Send me on my way so that I may go to my master.”

The answer is that she will go with the man. They ask, “Will you go with this man?” and she answers, “I will go…” (verse 58). The servant wants to leave now and her family wants ten days or so, and Rebekah is the one asked. Her answer is short and clear.

The answer is to be the mother of thousands. They say, “Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands.” (verse 60). That's the first part of their blessing. They go on to bless her offspring too.
The answer is True. Verse 61 says Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, mounted the camels, and followed the man. Then the servant took Rebekah and left. She doesn't leave alone.

The answer is camels. Verse 63 says Isaac, Abraham's son, went out to the field to meditate, and looking up, he saw the camels approaching. Those are the camels carrying Rebekah and her servant girls. I'd say that's quite the evening view.

The answer is veil. Verse 65 says, “So she took her veil and covered herself.” She had asked the servant who the man in the field was, and he said, “It is my master…” Her veil comes out as she learns it's Isaac.

The answer is comforted. Verse 67 says, “And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.” His mother was Sarah, and Isaac brought Rebekah into her tent. I think this is a tender line, so let's let it be tender.
